subject: DI04005021

body.en:
Definition / principle

Gas absorption transfers one or more components of a gas mixture into a contacting liquid solvent; desorption or stripping is the reverse transfer.

Detailed theory and conditions

Classification first: physical absorption dissolves a gas without an intended chemical reaction; chemical absorption couples dissolution with reaction in the liquid. Absorption may be single-component or multicomponent and batch or continuous. These are independent classifications. Chemical reaction can maintain a stronger driving force, but adds reagent demand, heat, regeneration and reaction-equilibrium requirements. Do not confuse absorption into a liquid bulk with adsorption onto a solid surface.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Gas mixture ના એક અથવા વધુ components ને contacting liquid solvent માં transfer કરવું એટલે gas absorption. Desorption/stripping તેની reverse transfer છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Classification: physical absorption માં intended chemical reaction વગર gas dissolve થાય છે. Chemical absorption માં dissolution સાથે liquid reaction જોડાય છે. Single/multicomponent તથા batch/continuous independent classifications છે. Reaction driving force જાળવી શકે છે, પરંતુ reagent, heat, regeneration તથા reaction-equilibrium requirements ઉમેરે છે. Liquid bulk absorption ને solid-surface adsorption સાથે ન ભેળવો.

body.en:
Definition / principle

An industrial absorption duty specifies the gas solute to recover or remove, the solvent and the required treated-gas and liquid-product quality.

Detailed theory and conditions

Examples include ammonia recovery into water, acid-gas treatment using a suitable reactive solvent and removal of soluble contaminants from process/off-gases. The solvent must match the actual gas chemistry: water is not universally suitable and a reactive scrubbing liquid produces a different waste/regeneration load from a physical solvent. The absorber may make a saleable solution, recover a valuable species, protect downstream equipment or meet emission targets. Feed variability, heat release, entrained mist, corrosion and solvent handling are part of the duty, not matters solved by a material balance alone.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Industrial absorption duty માં recover/remove કરવો તે gas solute, solvent તથા treated-gas/liquid-product quality નક્કી થાય છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Ammonia ને water માં recover કરવું, suitable reactive solvent થી acid-gas treatment તથા process/off-gas ના soluble contaminants દૂર કરવાં examples છે. Solvent actual chemistry મુજબ જોઈએ; water universal solvent નથી. Reactive scrubber તથા physical solvent ના waste/regeneration loads જુદા છે. Absorber saleable solution, valuable-species recovery, downstream protection અથવા emission control માટે હોઈ શકે છે. Feed variation, heat release, mist, corrosion તથા solvent handling ફક્ત material balance થી solve થતા નથી.

title.en: Gas solubility,equilibrium and effects of T/P
title.gu: Gas Solubility,Equilibrium તથા T/P ની અસર

h.en: Gas solubility,equilibrium and effects of T/P
h.gu: Gas Solubility,Equilibrium તથા T/P ની અસર

body.en:
Definition / principle

Gas solubility is the equilibrium dissolved amount under specified temperature, gas partial pressure and liquid composition. Henry’s law is a dilute-solution equilibrium relation with a stated convention.

Detailed theory and conditions

Use pA=HA xA in the pressure-per-mole-fraction convention; then yA*=HA xA/P. Higher solute partial pressure normally increases physical gas solubility at fixed temperature. Increasing total pressure at fixed gas mole fraction raises partial pressure; increasing total pressure while holding solute partial pressure fixed does not give the same solubility increase. For many physically absorbed gases, raising temperature reduces solubility because dissolution is exothermic, but the actual gas/solvent equilibrium data must decide; chemical reactions can change the trend. Nonlinear, concentrated or reactive systems may not obey a single Henry constant over the full range.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Specified temperature, gas partial pressure તથા liquid composition પર equilibrium dissolved amount એટલે gas solubility. Henry’s law stated convention ધરાવતી dilute-solution equilibrium relation છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Pressure-per-mole-fraction convention માં pA=HA xA એટલે yA*=HA xA/P લો. Fixed temperature પર solute partial pressure વધતાં physical solubility સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Gas mole fraction fixed રાખીને total pressure વધારવાથી partial pressure વધે છે; solute partial pressure fixed હોય તો સમાન solubility increase નહીં મળે. ઘણા physical systems માં dissolution exothermic હોવાથી temperature વધતાં solubility ઘટે છે, પરંતુ actual equilibrium data તપાસો. Reaction થી trend બદલાઈ શકે છે. Nonlinear/concentrated/reactive system માટે એક Henry constant સમગ્ર range માં valid ન હોઈ શકે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

title.en: Ideal liquid solution and Raoult’s law
title.gu: Ideal Liquid Solution તથા Raoult’s Law

h.en: Ideal liquid solution and Raoult’s law
h.gu: Ideal Liquid Solution તથા Raoult’s Law

body.en:
Definition / principle

An ideal liquid solution has unit activity coefficients on the Raoult-standard-state basis. Raoult’s law relates a volatile liquid component’s equilibrium partial pressure to its liquid mole fraction and pure-component saturation pressure.

Detailed theory and conditions

At a fixed temperature, pA*=xA pA, sat for an ideal liquid and an approximately ideal vapor. The saturation pressure depends strongly on temperature. The equilibrium gas fraction is pA*/P. The rule is not a universal solubility equation for every sparingly soluble or reacting gas; Henry’s dilute-solute standard state may be the appropriate description instead. Ideal mixing does not mean the contacting phases have identical compositions. A real activity coefficient or fugacity correction is needed when the stated ideal approximations fail.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Raoult standard-state basis પર activity coefficients unit હોય તે ideal liquid solution છે. Volatile liquid component ના equilibrium partial pressure ને liquid mole fraction તથા pure-component saturation pressure સાથે Raoult’s law જોડે છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Fixed temperature પર ideal liquid તથા approximately ideal vapor માટે pA*=xA pA, sat છે. Saturation pressure temperature પર ખૂબ આધારિત છે. Equilibrium gas fraction pA*/P છે. દરેક sparingly soluble/reacting gas માટે આ universal law નથી; dilute solute માટે Henry standard state વધુ યોગ્ય હોઈ શકે છે. Ideal mixing એટલે બંને phases ની compositions સમાન નહીં. Ideal assumptions fail થાય તો activity/fugacity corrections જોઈએ.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

body.en:
Definition / principle

A suitable absorption solvent provides sufficient selective capacity while remaining practical to circulate, separate, regenerate and handle safely.

Detailed theory and conditions

Consider high target-gas solubility/selectivity, low solvent volatility, manageable viscosity, chemical/thermal stability and low corrosiveness. Include toxicity, flammability, foaming, freezing point, availability, cost and compatibility with construction materials. Evaluate regeneration energy and the disposal/treatment of loaded solvent. Low volatility reduces solvent loss to gas; low viscosity aids transfer and pumping but cannot override poor selectivity. A reactive solvent may capture strongly while requiring heat removal and regeneration or reagent replacement. Do not select a solvent solely from the highest single equilibrium loading.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

પૂરતી selective capacity સાથે circulation, separation, regeneration તથા safe handling માટે practical હોય તે suitable absorption solvent છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

Target-gas solubility/selectivity, low volatility, manageable viscosity, chemical/thermal stability તથા low corrosion જુઓ. Toxicity, flammability, foaming, freezing point, availability, cost તથા material compatibility સામેલ કરો. Regeneration energy તથા loaded-solvent treatment/disposal ગણો. Low volatility solvent loss ઘટાડે છે. Low viscosity transfer/pumping ને મદદ કરે છે પણ poor selectivity સુધારતી નથી. Reactive solvent માં heat removal તથા regeneration/reagent replacement જોઈએ. ફક્ત સૌથી ઊંચી equilibrium loading પરથી solvent ન પસંદ કરો.

body.en:
Definition / principle

A solute-free flow is the flow of nontransferring carrier gas or solvent. Solute ratios Y and X are moles of solute per mole of carrier gas and solvent, respectively.

Detailed theory and conditions

For one-component transfer with negligible solvent evaporation, inert-gas dissolution and reaction, Vs and Ls remain constant even though total gas and liquid flows change. The displayed solute-free conversion ratios are not equal to mole fractions except approximately for dilute streams. Use the same molar time basis in all streams and label entering/exiting endpoints rather than relying on ambiguous subscripts. Henry’s linear y*=mx is not exactly linear in solute-free X, Y; use a converted relation or a clearly stated dilute approximation.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Solute-free flow એટલે nontransferring carrier gas અથવા solvent નો flow. Y તથા X અનુક્રમે carrier-gas mole તથા solvent mole દીઠ solute moles છે.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

એક-component transfer અને negligible solvent evaporation, inert-gas dissolution તથા reaction માટે Vs, Ls constant રહે છે, જ્યારે total flows બદલાઈ શકે છે. Displayed solute-free conversion ratios dilute approximation સિવાય mole fractions સમાન નથી. બધા streams માટે same molar/time basis લો અને endpoints entering/exiting પ્રમાણે label કરો. Henry નું linear y*=mx exact solute-free X, Y માં linear નથી; converted relation અથવા સ્પષ્ટ dilute approximation લો.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady, nonreacting, one transferred solute; constant carrier flows Vs and Ls; negligible solvent volatility and inert-gas dissolution. All X, Y are solute-free molar ratios.

  1. Overall solute balance: gas enters rich and leaves lean; liquid enters lean and leaves rich.

  2. Rearrange to amount transferred.

  3. Take a top-to-local-section balance. Gas leaving the top has Yout and liquid entering the top has Xin.

  4. Obtain the positive-slope operating line. Endpoints are (Xin, Yout) and (Xout, Yin).

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: stream labels → overall balance → rearrange → operating-line endpoints. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.
body.gu:
સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady, nonreacting, એક transferred solute, constant carrier flows Vs, Ls તથા negligible solvent volatility/inert dissolution લો. X, Y solute-free molar ratios છે.

  1. Gas rich→lean તથા liquid lean→rich માટે overall solute balance.

  2. Transferred amount પ્રમાણે rearrange કરો.

  3. Top થી local section સુધી balance લો. Top gas Yout તથા liquid Xin છે.

  4. Positive-slope operating line મેળવો. Endpoints (Xin, Yout) તથા (Xout, Yin) છે.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

Steady, nonreacting, one transferred solute; constant carrier flows Vs and Ls; negligible solvent volatility and inert-gas dissolution. All X, Y are solute-free molar ratios.

  1. Both streams enter the same end with Yin and Xin.

  2. Rearrange at any common position.

  3. The local operating line has negative slope on this X, Y plot.

  4. At the common outlet the overall transferred amount is unchanged in balance form, but endpoint pairing and achievable approach differ.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: common inlet → local balance → negative operating-line slope → outlet balance. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.
body.gu:
સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Steady, nonreacting, એક transferred solute, constant carrier flows Vs, Ls તથા negligible solvent volatility/inert dissolution લો. X, Y solute-free molar ratios છે.

  1. બંને streams same end પર Yin તથા Xin સાથે enter થાય છે.

  2. કોઈ પણ common position માટે rearrange કરો.

  3. આ X, Y plot પર local operating-line slope negative છે.

  4. Common outlet પર overall balance form સમાન છે, પરંતુ endpoint pairing તથા attainable approach જુદાં છે.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

body.en:
Symbols, model and assumptions

Use the preceding constant-carrier countercurrent model. Specified Yin, Yout and Xin; given equilibrium curve. A bottom pinch formula is valid only when that pinch controls. Check interior tangency and the whole operating range.

  1. Start from the overall transfer balance.

  2. Minimum solvent corresponds to the largest thermodynamically admissible outlet loading for a bottom-controlled pinch.

  3. Insert the limiting loading.

  4. Only if the given equilibrium model is linear in solute-free ratios, solve Xout, max explicitly.

  5. At minimum a pinch eliminates local driving force and finite-rate equipment becomes unbounded in the ideal model. Actual ratio must exceed the feasible minimum.

4-mark / 7-mark study depth

4-mark path: overall balance → identify controlling equilibrium pinch → limiting ratio; qualify bottom-pinch assumption. For a full7-mark format reproduce all intermediate steps and conditions. These are study formats, not guaranteed official question marks.
body.gu:
સંકેતો, Model તથા Assumptions

Constant-carrier countercurrent model તથા specified Yin, Yout, Xin અને equilibrium curve લો. Bottom pinch formula ત્યારે જ લો જ્યારે તે controlling હોય. Interior tangency તથા સમગ્ર range તપાસો.

  1. Overall transfer balance લો.

  2. Bottom-controlled pinch માટે minimum solvent એટલે સૌથી મોટી thermodynamically admissible outlet loading.

  3. Limiting loading મૂકો.

  4. આપેલું equilibrium model solute-free ratios માં linear હોય ત્યારે જ Xout, max આ રીતે લો.

  5. Minimum પર pinch ની local driving force zero થાય છે અને ideal finite-rate model માં required size અનંત તરફ જાય છે. Actual ratio feasible minimum કરતાં વધુ લો.

4-mark / 7-mark Study Depth

4-mark માટે necessary assumptions, governing equation, મુખ્ય integration/balance તથા boxed result આપો. Full7-mark format માટે બધા intermediate steps તથા conditions લખો. આ study formats છે; official marks ની ખાતરી નથી.

body.en:
Definition / principle

Height Equivalent to a Theoretical Plate is the active packed height that gives separation equivalent to one theoretical equilibrium stage for specified conditions.

Detailed theory and conditions

If N theoretical stages represent a specified packed-bed separation, active packed height Z=N×HETP. HETP is a performance equivalence, not the physical tray spacing and not a universal property of packing alone. It depends on the mixture, loading, wetting, distribution and operating conditions. Overall vessel height includes additional space for distributors, demisters and disengagement, so it is larger than the active packed height. HETP should not be confused with a height of transfer unit; the syllabus asks HETP, not an unrelated full HTU/NTU design derivation.

Equations and notation
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા / સિદ્ધાંત

Specified conditions પર એક theoretical equilibrium stage જેટલું separation આપતી active packed height એટલે Height Equivalent to a Theoretical Plate, HETP.

વિગતવાર Theory તથા Conditions

N theoretical stages જેટલા separation માટે active packed height Z=N×HETP છે. HETP physical tray spacing નથી તથા packing ની એકલ universal property નથી. Mixture, loading, wetting, distribution તથા conditions પર આધારિત છે. Distributors, demisters તથા disengagement માટે વધારાની જગ્યા હોવાથી total vessel height active packing કરતાં વધુ હોય છે. HETP ને height of transfer unit સાથે ન ભેળવો; અહીં syllabus મુજબ HETP છે.

સમીકરણો તથા Notation

body.en:
Definition

A vertical gas–liquid contactor with trays that repeatedly disperse rising gas through flowing liquid.

Principle

Interfacial contact on each tray transfers soluble gas toward the liquid; successive trays approximate a stagewise countercurrent cascade.

Construction

The vertical shell contains horizontal trays with gas passages, liquid weirs and downcomers. A sieve-tray arrangement is illustrated; valve and bubble-cap trays are alternatives. The gas inlet is near the bottom and lean solvent enters above the upper tray. Treated gas leaves the top, commonly through a mist eliminator, while rich liquid leaves a bottom sump. Downcomer outlets maintain suitable liquid seals, and access/supports allow inspection. Trays provide distinct contacting levels rather than a continuous packed surface.

Working

Rising gas passes through tray openings and bubbles through the retained liquid. Liquid flows across a tray, over its weir and down the downcomer to the next lower tray. Solute crosses the gas–liquid interface, so gas becomes leaner upward and liquid richer downward. Sufficient gas supports effective contact; too little can cause weeping, whereas excessive gas/liquid loading can cause entrainment or flooding. Actual tray departures need not reach equilibrium. Although both feeds flow continuously, the contacting is stagewise; the syllabus grouping under continuous equipment refers to throughput, not differential contact.

Applications

Gas purification/recovery where tray operation, inspection and staged contact are suitable.

Limitations and precautions

Pressure drop, foaming, corrosion, weeping and flooding limit operation; equipment must remain within its approved hydraulic and pressure envelope.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Rising gas ને flowing liquid માં વારંવાર disperse કરવા trays ધરાવતો vertical gas–liquid contactor છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

દરેક tray પર interfacial contact થી soluble gas liquid તરફ transfer થાય છે. Successive trays stagewise countercurrent cascade બનાવે છે.

રચના (Construction)

Vertical shell માં horizontal trays, gas passages, liquid weirs તથા downcomers છે. Drawing sieve-tray arrangement બતાવે છે; valve તથા bubble-cap alternatives છે. Gas નીચે enter થાય છે અને lean solvent upper tray ઉપરથી આવે છે. Treated gas top mist eliminator તરફથી તથા rich liquid bottom sump માંથી નીકળે છે. Downcomer outlet liquid seal જાળવે છે. Supports/access inspection માટે છે. Trays distinct contacting levels આપે છે, continuous packed surface નહીં.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Gas openings માંથી ઊઠીને retained liquid માં bubbles બનાવે છે. Liquid tray ઉપરથી weir પાર કરીને downcomer વડે lower tray પર જાય છે. Interface પરથી solute transfer થતાં ઉપર જતો gas lean અને નીચે જતું liquid rich બને છે. Low gas થી weeping તથા excessive loading થી entrainment/flooding થઈ શકે છે. Actual departures equilibrium સુધી પહોંચે જ એવું નથી. બંને feeds continuous છે પણ contacting stagewise છે; syllabus નું continuous-equipment grouping throughput માટે છે, differential contact માટે નહીં.

ઉપયોગો

Suitable tray operation/inspection સાથે gas purification તથા recovery.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Pressure drop, foaming, corrosion, weeping તથા flooding limits છે. Approved hydraulic/pressure envelope જરૂરી છે.

body.en:
Definition

A vertical gas–liquid contactor containing packing that supplies wetted area for differential interphase transfer.

Principle

Gas and liquid contact countercurrently over distributed wetted packing surfaces; local driving force changes with height.

Construction

The shell contains random or structured packing retained by supports and hold-down arrangements. A top liquid distributor spreads lean solvent; redistributors may serve deep beds. Gas enters below the packing and leaves above it through a disengagement/mist-removal region. Rich liquid drains into a bottom sump and outlet. Packing must provide area and void space without blocking phase passage. Appropriate materials, inspection access and distribution are as important as nominal surface area.

Working

Solvent flows downward as films and rivulets while gas rises through the voids. Soluble gas transfers across repeatedly renewed interfaces; the liquid gains solute toward the bottom and gas loses solute toward the top. There are no physical equilibrium trays, so composition varies progressively along the active bed. Poor distribution creates channeling and dry areas, while excessive loading raises pressure drop and can flood the bed. Distributors therefore maintain useful area rather than allowing liquid to run only near the wall.

Applications

Absorption duties benefiting from high wetted area and often relatively low pressure drop.

Limitations and precautions

Maldistribution, fouling, plugging, foaming and flooding are limitations. Packing choice alone does not guarantee mass-transfer performance.
body.gu:
વ્યાખ્યા

Wetted area પર differential interphase transfer આપવા packing ધરાવતો vertical gas–liquid contactor છે.

સિદ્ધાંત

Wetted packing surfaces પર gas/liquid countercurrent contact કરે છે. Local driving force height પ્રમાણે બદલાય છે.

રચના (Construction)

Shell માં supports/hold-down સાથે random અથવા structured packing હોય છે. Top distributor lean solvent ફેલાવે છે. Deep bed માં redistributors હોઈ શકે છે. Gas packing નીચે enter થઈ top disengagement/mist-removal region માંથી બહાર જાય છે. Rich liquid bottom sump/outlet માં drain થાય છે. Packing area તથા void space આપે છે. Material, inspection તથા distribution nominal surface area જેટલાં મહત્વનાં છે.

કાર્યપદ્ધતિ (Working)

Solvent films/rivulets તરીકે નીચે અને gas voids માંથી ઉપર જાય છે. Renewed interfaces પર gas solute liquid માં જાય છે. Bottom તરફ liquid rich તથા top તરફ gas lean થાય છે. Physical equilibrium trays નથી; active bed દરમિયાન composition સતત બદલાય છે. Poor distribution થી channeling/dry area તથા excessive loading થી pressure-drop/flooding થાય છે. Distributor liquid ને ફક્ત wall પાસે વહેવા દેવાને બદલે useful area જાળવે છે.

ઉપયોગો

High wetted area તથા ઘણી વખત low pressure drop યોગ્ય હોય તેવી absorption duties.

Limitations તથા Precautions

Maldistribution, fouling, plugging, foaming તથા flooding limits છે. ફક્ત packing choice performance ની ખાતરી નથી.

h.en: Rate of gas absorption in a packed tower
h.gu: Packed Tower માં Gas Absorption Rate

body.en:
Objective and official scope

Find the absorbed-solute molar rate from measured steady gas/liquid streams in the approved packed-tower trainer.

Apparatus and preparation

Approved gas/solvent system, tower trainer, flowmeters, T/P indicators, gas-composition analyzer and validated liquid assay. Inspect the trainer diagram and range before supervised use.

Principle and assumptions

Use component balances with compatible molar flow and composition bases. Total gas flow may change as solute is absorbed. Constant inert-carrier Vs requires negligible inert dissolution/solvent evaporation.

Procedure and record

Under the approved start-up/shutdown SOP establish the assigned stable operating condition. Record both inlet/outlet compositions and calibrated flows with T/P and sample IDs. Observe pressure drop and liquid distribution without entering or modifying the tower. Compare gas loss with liquid gain, accounting for sample losses and any reaction stoichiometry. Report discrepancies rather than adjusting readings to force closure.

Calculation format

Safety, quality and limitations

Use only the institution-approved gas and treatment/vent system. No toxic-gas generation, pressurization or live valve changes outside the supervised SOP. A rate balance alone does not give a mass-transfer coefficient without area/driving-force information.

Blank observation sheet—record actual readings only

Run, T, PGas in/out flowyin, youtLiquid in/outAssayΔP
——————
——————

Result: to be calculated from signed laboratory observations; no performance or experiment completion is claimed.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Types of gas absorption.
q.gu: Gas Absorption ના પ્રકાર ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Gas absorption transfers one or more components of a gas mixture into a contacting liquid solvent; desorption or stripping is the reverse transfer. Classification first: physical absorption dissolves a gas without an intended chemical reaction; chemical absorption couples dissolution with reaction in the liquid. Absorption may be single-component or multicomponent and batch or continuous. These are independent classifications. Chemical reaction can maintain a stronger driving force, but adds reagent demand, heat, regeneration and reaction-equilibrium requirements. Do not confuse absorption into a liquid bulk with adsorption onto a solid surface.
a.gu: Gas mixture ના એક અથવા વધુ components ને contacting liquid solvent માં transfer કરવું એટલે gas absorption. Desorption/stripping તેની reverse transfer છે. Classification: physical absorption માં intended chemical reaction વગર gas dissolve થાય છે. Chemical absorption માં dissolution સાથે liquid reaction જોડાય છે. Single/multicomponent તથા batch/continuous independent classifications છે. Reaction driving force જાળવી શકે છે, પરંતુ reagent, heat, regeneration તથા reaction-equilibrium requirements ઉમેરે છે. Liquid bulk absorption ને solid-surface adsorption સાથે ન ભેળવો.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Industrial applications of absorption.
q.gu: Absorption ના Industrial Applications ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: An industrial absorption duty specifies the gas solute to recover or remove, the solvent and the required treated-gas and liquid-product quality. Examples include ammonia recovery into water, acid-gas treatment using a suitable reactive solvent and removal of soluble contaminants from process/off-gases. The solvent must match the actual gas chemistry: water is not universally suitable and a reactive scrubbing liquid produces a different waste/regeneration load from a physical solvent. The absorber may make a saleable solution, recover a valuable species, protect downstream equipment or meet emission targets. Feed variability, heat release, entrained mist, corrosion and solvent handling are part of the duty, not matters solved by a material balance alone.
a.gu: Industrial absorption duty માં recover/remove કરવો તે gas solute, solvent તથા treated-gas/liquid-product quality નક્કી થાય છે. Ammonia ને water માં recover કરવું, suitable reactive solvent થી acid-gas treatment તથા process/off-gas ના soluble contaminants દૂર કરવાં examples છે. Solvent actual chemistry મુજબ જોઈએ; water universal solvent નથી. Reactive scrubber તથા physical solvent ના waste/regeneration loads જુદા છે. Absorber saleable solution, valuable-species recovery, downstream protection અથવા emission control માટે હોઈ શકે છે. Feed variation, heat release, mist, corrosion તથા solvent handling ફક્ત material balance થી solve થતા નથી.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Gas solubility,equilibrium and effects of T/P.
q.gu: Gas Solubility,Equilibrium તથા T/P ની અસર ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Gas solubility is the equilibrium dissolved amount under specified temperature, gas partial pressure and liquid composition. Henry’s law is a dilute-solution equilibrium relation with a stated convention. Use pA=HA xA in the pressure-per-mole-fraction convention; then yA*=HA xA/P. Higher solute partial pressure normally increases physical gas solubility at fixed temperature. Increasing total pressure at fixed gas mole fraction raises partial pressure; increasing total pressure while holding solute partial pressure fixed does not give the same solubility increase. For many physically absorbed gases, raising temperature reduces solubility because dissolution is exothermic, but the actual gas/solvent equilibrium data must decide; chemical reactions can change the trend. Nonlinear, concentrated or reactive systems may not obey a single Henry constant over the full range.
a.gu: Specified temperature, gas partial pressure તથા liquid composition પર equilibrium dissolved amount એટલે gas solubility. Henry’s law stated convention ધરાવતી dilute-solution equilibrium relation છે. Pressure-per-mole-fraction convention માં pA=HA xA એટલે yA*=HA xA/P લો. Fixed temperature પર solute partial pressure વધતાં physical solubility સામાન્ય રીતે વધે છે. Gas mole fraction fixed રાખીને total pressure વધારવાથી partial pressure વધે છે; solute partial pressure fixed હોય તો સમાન solubility increase નહીં મળે. ઘણા physical systems માં dissolution exothermic હોવાથી temperature વધતાં solubility ઘટે છે, પરંતુ actual equilibrium data તપાસો. Reaction થી trend બદલાઈ શકે છે. Nonlinear/concentrated/reactive system માટે એક Henry constant સમગ્ર range માં valid ન હોઈ શકે.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Ideal liquid solution and Raoult’s law.
q.gu: Ideal Liquid Solution તથા Raoult’s Law ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: An ideal liquid solution has unit activity coefficients on the Raoult-standard-state basis. Raoult’s law relates a volatile liquid component’s equilibrium partial pressure to its liquid mole fraction and pure-component saturation pressure. At a fixed temperature, pA*=xA pA, sat for an ideal liquid and an approximately ideal vapor. The saturation pressure depends strongly on temperature. The equilibrium gas fraction is pA*/P. The rule is not a universal solubility equation for every sparingly soluble or reacting gas; Henry’s dilute-solute standard state may be the appropriate description instead. Ideal mixing does not mean the contacting phases have identical compositions. A real activity coefficient or fugacity correction is needed when the stated ideal approximations fail.
a.gu: Raoult standard-state basis પર activity coefficients unit હોય તે ideal liquid solution છે. Volatile liquid component ના equilibrium partial pressure ને liquid mole fraction તથા pure-component saturation pressure સાથે Raoult’s law જોડે છે. Fixed temperature પર ideal liquid તથા approximately ideal vapor માટે pA*=xA pA, sat છે. Saturation pressure temperature પર ખૂબ આધારિત છે. Equilibrium gas fraction pA*/P છે. દરેક sparingly soluble/reacting gas માટે આ universal law નથી; dilute solute માટે Henry standard state વધુ યોગ્ય હોઈ શકે છે. Ideal mixing એટલે બંને phases ની compositions સમાન નહીં. Ideal assumptions fail થાય તો activity/fugacity corrections જોઈએ.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Choice of absorption solvent.
q.gu: Absorption Solvent ની પસંદગી ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A suitable absorption solvent provides sufficient selective capacity while remaining practical to circulate, separate, regenerate and handle safely. Consider high target-gas solubility/selectivity, low solvent volatility, manageable viscosity, chemical/thermal stability and low corrosiveness. Include toxicity, flammability, foaming, freezing point, availability, cost and compatibility with construction materials. Evaluate regeneration energy and the disposal/treatment of loaded solvent. Low volatility reduces solvent loss to gas; low viscosity aids transfer and pumping but cannot override poor selectivity. A reactive solvent may capture strongly while requiring heat removal and regeneration or reagent replacement. Do not select a solvent solely from the highest single equilibrium loading.
a.gu: પૂરતી selective capacity સાથે circulation, separation, regeneration તથા safe handling માટે practical હોય તે suitable absorption solvent છે. Target-gas solubility/selectivity, low volatility, manageable viscosity, chemical/thermal stability તથા low corrosion જુઓ. Toxicity, flammability, foaming, freezing point, availability, cost તથા material compatibility સામેલ કરો. Regeneration energy તથા loaded-solvent treatment/disposal ગણો. Low volatility solvent loss ઘટાડે છે. Low viscosity transfer/pumping ને મદદ કરે છે પણ poor selectivity સુધારતી નથી. Reactive solvent માં heat removal તથા regeneration/reagent replacement જોઈએ. ફક્ત સૌથી ઊંચી equilibrium loading પરથી solvent ન પસંદ કરો.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Solute-free material-balance basis.
q.gu: Solute-free Material-balance Basis ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A solute-free flow is the flow of nontransferring carrier gas or solvent. Solute ratios Y and X are moles of solute per mole of carrier gas and solvent, respectively. For one-component transfer with negligible solvent evaporation, inert-gas dissolution and reaction, Vs and Ls remain constant even though total gas and liquid flows change. The displayed solute-free conversion ratios are not equal to mole fractions except approximately for dilute streams. Use the same molar time basis in all streams and label entering/exiting endpoints rather than relying on ambiguous subscripts. Henry’s linear y*=mx is not exactly linear in solute-free X, Y; use a converted relation or a clearly stated dilute approximation.
a.gu: Solute-free flow એટલે nontransferring carrier gas અથવા solvent નો flow. Y તથા X અનુક્રમે carrier-gas mole તથા solvent mole દીઠ solute moles છે. એક-component transfer અને negligible solvent evaporation, inert-gas dissolution તથા reaction માટે Vs, Ls constant રહે છે, જ્યારે total flows બદલાઈ શકે છે. Displayed solute-free conversion ratios dilute approximation સિવાય mole fractions સમાન નથી. બધા streams માટે same molar/time basis લો અને endpoints entering/exiting પ્રમાણે label કરો. Henry નું linear y*=mx exact solute-free X, Y માં linear નથી; converted relation અથવા સ્પષ્ટ dilute approximation લો.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of HETP and its proper use.
q.gu: HETP તથા તેનો યોગ્ય ઉપયોગ ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: Height Equivalent to a Theoretical Plate is the active packed height that gives separation equivalent to one theoretical equilibrium stage for specified conditions. If N theoretical stages represent a specified packed-bed separation, active packed height Z=N×HETP. HETP is a performance equivalence, not the physical tray spacing and not a universal property of packing alone. It depends on the mixture, loading, wetting, distribution and operating conditions. Overall vessel height includes additional space for distributors, demisters and disengagement, so it is larger than the active packed height. HETP should not be confused with a height of transfer unit; the syllabus asks HETP, not an unrelated full HTU/NTU design derivation.
a.gu: Specified conditions પર એક theoretical equilibrium stage જેટલું separation આપતી active packed height એટલે Height Equivalent to a Theoretical Plate, HETP. N theoretical stages જેટલા separation માટે active packed height Z=N×HETP છે. HETP physical tray spacing નથી તથા packing ની એકલ universal property નથી. Mixture, loading, wetting, distribution તથા conditions પર આધારિત છે. Distributors, demisters તથા disengagement માટે વધારાની જગ્યા હોવાથી total vessel height active packing કરતાં વધુ હોય છે. HETP ને height of transfer unit સાથે ન ભેળવો; અહીં syllabus મુજબ HETP છે.

q.en: Define and explain the principle of Tray tower absorber.
q.gu: Tray Tower Absorber ની વ્યાખ્યા તથા principle સમજાવો.

a.en: A vertical gas–liquid contactor with trays that repeatedly disperse rising gas through flowing liquid. Interfacial contact on each tray transfers soluble gas toward the liquid; successive trays approximate a stagewise countercurrent cascade.
